name: Israel at Baal-peor
charge: Fornication with the daughters of Moab; sacrificing to their gods
summary: In Shittim the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods. Israel ate, bowed down, and joined himself unto Baal-peor. The plague took twenty-four thousand.
offense: It was Balaam's counsel executed. He could not curse a people God had blessed, so he taught Balak the one thing that works: put another god in front of Israel and send the women to bring them to it (Numbers 31:16; Revelation 2:14). Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab (Numbers 25:1), and they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods (Numbers 25:2). The whoredom and the worship were not two sins but one; the rite of Baal-peor was whoredom, and Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:3), joined as a man is joined to a wife. Hosea gives the verdict on the whole affair: they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according as they loved (Hosea 9:10), and the psalm adds what they ate: they joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead (Psalms 106:28). It was the golden calf again, for the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play, and that play was the same play (1 Corinthians 10:7-8).
judgment: The Lord's sentence began with the leadership: take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel (Numbers 25:4), and Moses said unto the judges of Israel, slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal-peor (Numbers 25:5), every judge by his rank  taking the men under him. A plague ran through the camp while the sentence was being carried out, and it was stayed by the javelin of Phinehas, which is entered separately as a blessing, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand (Numbers 25:9). Paul, counting the day itself, says three and twenty thousand fell in one day (1 Corinthians 10:8). Moses set the outcome before the next generation as a thing their own eyes had seen: all the men that followed Baal-peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you, but ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day (Deuteronomy 4:3-4). Then the judgment turned outward against the nation that had supplied the women, which is entered under the Midianites.

verses.text: And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.
And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.
And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.
Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal–peor: for all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them from among you.
They joined themselves also unto Baal–peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them.

I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baal–peor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved.
Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

lawDetails.text: Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.

entries.commentary: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ. Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Let us now praise famous men: Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel; therefore a covenant of peace was made with him, that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel. That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes. The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.

The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25); go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

A thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed for war, were sent with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25).

They warred against the Midianites as the Lord commanded Moses, slew all the males, and slew the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba. Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

Israel took the women of Midian captives with their little ones, took the spoil of all their cattle, flocks, and goods, and burnt all their cities and all their goodly castles with fire. Midian comes from the lineage of Ishmael, the people known today as the Arab man. This shows Esau was not the one who first came up with castles; the castles seen in the movies were conquered from other nations. They took all the spoil and all the prey, both of men and of beasts: the Midianites had captives of their own, and Israel took over both the men and the beasts when they overcame them.

Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, the leaders of the army of Israel, because they saved all the women alive. These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of [Numbers 25](/bible/numbers/25). Therefore every male among the little ones was to be killed, and every woman that had known man by lying with him; but the women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

Whoever killed any person or touched any slain had to abide without the camp seven days and purify himself and his captives on the third day and on the seventh day. That is the law going back to [Numbers 5:2](/bible/numbers/5#v2), putting the defiled outside the camp. Purifying the raiment, all that is made of skins, all work of goats' hair, and all things made of wood goes back to the law of purification in [Numbers 19](/bible/numbers/19). Eleazar the priest gave the ordinance: gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead, everything that may abide the fire, goes through the fire and is purified with the water of separation; whatever abides not the fire goes through the water; and on the seventh day they wash their clothes, are clean, and come into the camp.

Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation took the sum of the prey, both of man and of beast, adding up all that was taken from the Midianites. The prey was divided into two parts: between the army who went out to battle and took the prey, and all the congregation that did not go to war. The nation looked out for each other. A tribute was levied unto the Lord: of the men of war, one soul of five hundred, of persons, beeves, asses, and sheep, given to Eleazar the priest for a heave offering, because he was the priest; and of the children of Israel's half, one portion of fifty, given to the Levites which kept the charge of the tabernacle.

Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

Hearken, O Israel: hearken means listen, pay attention, and there is a difference between hearing and listening. The statutes and judgments are taught for to do them; knowing you are an Israelite is only half the battle. The main thing is applying the scriptures, doing what the Most High is telling you to do, that ye may live. The promise is to go in and possess the land, and possessing land is true wealth: your milk and honey, your cattle, your agriculture, where you cultivate and take care of your family. It is not the diamonds, the cars, the sneakers, or the newest phone; a big house with no land is not wealth, and that is why the heathen boxes our people into apartments.

Ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish ought from it. This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book: the prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ, and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes. The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove [Matthew 18:11](/bible/matthew/18#v11) and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

Your eyes have seen what the Lord did because of Baal-peor: all the men that followed Baal-peor were destroyed from among the people, and this recalls the history of Balaam. Balaam was a Midianite, an Ishmaelite. But ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day: those who said they would not go after that foolishness were saved alive. The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

Keep therefore and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations. Israel deals with the Almighty; having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at. When Israel keeps the laws it makes them a peculiar nation: peculiar by definition means characteristic of only one person, group, or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations. Royal means of a kingly ancestry, and the King of kings is Christ; but rulership belongs to the lineage only when the laws are kept. When Israel is fallen into sin, the people look worse than the nations instead of wise and understanding. Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

What nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them? The Most High is near unto Israel in all things they call upon him for, and no nation has statutes and judgments so righteous as this law. When Israel keeps the laws, statutes, and commandments, they are the light of the world; in the days when the brothers and sisters were in order, the nations looked on and marveled at what nation this was, so great and so beautiful.

Take heed to thyself and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things thine eyes have seen; and teach them thy sons, and thy sons' sons. These are generational commandments: children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Why learn to fear the Most High? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

The mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, and the Most High spake out of the midst of the fire; ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude. He declared his covenant, even ten commandments: the ten are the umbrella over all the other commandments, the sub-laws and sub-statutes beneath them. And he wrote them upon two tables of stone. The laws men call the mosaic laws did not belong to Moses; they were written with the finger of God and given to Israel by Christ, and they endure for ever.

The Most High commanded Moses at that time to teach the statutes and judgments, and Israel is charged to take good heed, for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day the Lord spake in Horeb. No similitude means he spoke plainly and clearly, not in dark speeches: when the commandments were given there was no arguing over what they meant. Fringes on the borders of the garments, no swine, thou shalt not kill; it was simple and easy to understand. Lest ye corrupt yourselves and make a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female: Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The likeness of any beast on the earth goes back to idols like Heqet the frog god and Sobek the god of the river; the likeness of any winged fowl to Horus the falcon; anything that creepeth on the ground to the beetles, flies, and locusts they deified; any fish in the waters to Sobek and to Dagon the fish god of the Babylonians, whose symbolism carries into pagan imagery to this day. The eagle and the falcon symbols of the powers of this world trace back to the gods and goddesses of Egypt, because this present power is spiritual Egypt and takes after her. Lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven and be driven to worship the sun, the moon, and the stars: that is Ra the sun god and Nut the sky goddess, and it is also astrology, the zodiac, and witchcraft today. Calling yourself a Gemini or a Taurus is the same star worship; none of it is the way to the kingdom, and it was filth learned in Egypt. Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

The Lord hath taken you and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance. Furthermore the Lord was angry with me for your sakes: again Moses lays his barred crossing on the people. It is how the workers feel when they go out to preach truth and catch anger for it; you are not arguing with the messenger, you are mad at the Bible, so speak the oracles and neither add nor diminish to please anybody. Moses must die in this land and not go over Jordan, but ye shall go over and possess that good land; he kept repeating it, longing for what he would not see.

Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant and make a graven image, for the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When children's children are begotten and the stay in the land grows long, corruption creeps in; make the graven image and do evil to provoke him, and ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land. Heaven and earth are called to witness against Israel this day; the warning was on record before it ever came to pass.

And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen: this is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul; the seeking begins with the spirit of fear, to get right with the Most High. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days: the latter days began when Christ came, for God who spake in time past by the prophets hath in these last days spoken by his Son. And shalt be obedient unto his voice: the voice of the Most High tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High. For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

Ask now of the days that are past, since the day that God created man upon the earth: you are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only, but the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it. Did ever people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and live? Hath God assayed to take him a nation from the midst of another nation, by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand? There is no such history anywhere else; the Most High did this for Israel alone. Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee; and because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out of Egypt in his sight with his mighty power. To drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou art: they had more economic might and more military power, but the Most High delivered Israel out of their hands, and to this day the twelve tribes are still here. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else. Consider is the key word: really appreciate all of it, for Israel could have been born of any nation, but the Most High ordained this people, and the way to cash in is simply keeping the commandments.

Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes and his commandments, that it may go well with thee and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth. This is the solution. The voting, protesting, and marching have never worked and never will; trust in the Most High and keep his laws, and he will take care of his people with long days, families, and the land.

Then Moses severed three cities on this side Jordan toward the sunrising, that the slayer which killed his neighbour unawares, and hated him not in times past, might flee thither and live: Bezer in the wilderness for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites. The chapter closes with the summary: this is the law, the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which Moses spake unto the children of Israel after they came forth out of Egypt, in the land of Sihon and of Og, the two kings of the Amorites.

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

lawsResolved.text: Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.
It is the will of God that you abstain from fornication and sexual immorality.
Do not covenant with the heathen or their gods, or keep company with the heathen and idolaters.
We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
Death penalty is to be given to idolaters.
A church is not to have those within it who hold to the doctrine of Balaam.
